# Data Munging

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)

project_folder <- "/Users/purnagamage/Documents/GitHub/DS-Corps-Assessents"

folder <- file.path(
  project_folder,
  "all_variables_needed"
)

week4_folder <- file.path(
  project_folder,
  "Week_4"
)

dir.create(
  week4_folder,
  showWarnings = FALSE,
  recursive = TRUE
)

files <- c(
  "AI_historical_data.csv",
  "GOOGL_historical_data.csv",
  "MSFT_historical_data.csv",
  "NVDA_historical_data.csv",
  "all_capex_ppi_daily_interpolated.csv",
  "GT_jobs_int.csv",
  "GT_skills_int.csv",
  "indeed_data_analysis.csv",
  "indeed-all.csv",
  "indeed-software.csv"
)

read_file <- function(filename) {

  data <- read_csv(
    file.path(folder, filename),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

  # Find the date column
  date_col <- names(data)[
    grepl("date|month|time", names(data), ignore.case = TRUE)
  ][1]

  if (is.na(date_col)) {
    stop("No date column found in: ", filename)
  }

  # Convert the date
  date_values <- as.character(data[[date_col]])

  parsed_dates <- suppressWarnings(
    as.Date(
      parse_date_time(
        date_values,
        orders = c(
          "ymd",
          "mdy",
          "dmy",
          "ym",
          "my",
          "Ymd",
          "bY",
          "BY",
          "bdy",
          "Ymd HMS",
          "ymd HMS"
        )
      )
    )
  )

  if (all(is.na(parsed_dates))) {
    stop(
      "Dates could not be read in: ",
      filename,
      "\nFirst date values: ",
      paste(head(date_values), collapse = ", ")
    )
  }

  # Rename the date column
  names(data)[names(data) == date_col] <- "Date"
  data$Date <- parsed_dates

  # Remove rows with missing dates
  data <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(Date))

  # Add filename to the other column names
  file_name <- make.names(
    tools::file_path_sans_ext(filename)
  )

  data %>%
    rename_with(
      ~ paste0(file_name, "_", .x),
      -Date
    )
}

# Load the files
data_list <- lapply(files, read_file)

# Find the common overlapping period
common_start <- as.Date(
  max(sapply(data_list, function(x) as.numeric(min(x$Date)))),
  origin = "1970-01-01"
)

common_end <- as.Date(
  min(sapply(data_list, function(x) as.numeric(max(x$Date)))),
  origin = "1970-01-01"
)

# Combine all datasets by date
combined_data <- reduce(
  data_list,
  full_join,
  by = "Date"
) %>%
  filter(
    Date >= common_start,
    Date <= common_end
  ) %>%
  arrange(Date)
```

```{r}
# Maximum CCF lag in days
lag_max <- 36

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Functions for selecting columns
# ------------------------------------------------------------

get_numeric_columns <- function(pattern) {
  
  columns <- grep(
    pattern,
    names(combined_data),
    value = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )
  
  if (length(columns) == 0) {
    return(character(0))
  }
  
  numeric_columns <- vapply(
    columns,
    function(column_name) {
      is.numeric(combined_data[[column_name]])
    },
    logical(1)
  )
  
  return(columns[numeric_columns])
}


get_job_column <- function(pattern) {
  
  columns <- get_numeric_columns(pattern)
  
  if (length(columns) == 0) {
    return(NA_character_)
  }
  
  preferred <- columns[
    grepl(
      "main[._]?value|job.*opening|posting.*index|value",
      columns,
      ignore.case = TRUE
    )
  ]
  
  if (length(preferred) > 0) {
    return(preferred[1])
  }
  
  return(columns[1])
}


get_stock_column <- function(pattern) {
  
  columns <- get_numeric_columns(pattern)
  
  if (length(columns) == 0) {
    return(NA_character_)
  }
  
  # Prefer adjusted closing price
  preferred <- columns[
    grepl(
      "adj.*close|adjusted.*close",
      columns,
      ignore.case = TRUE
    )
  ]
  
  # Otherwise use another closing-price column
  if (length(preferred) == 0) {
    preferred <- columns[
      grepl(
        "close",
        columns,
        ignore.case = TRUE
      )
    ]
  }
  
  if (length(preferred) > 0) {
    return(preferred[1])
  }
  
  return(columns[1])
}
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Create one regularly spaced daily dataset
# ------------------------------------------------------------

needed_columns <- unique(
  c(
    "Date",
    unname(job_columns),
    unname(predictor_columns)
  )
)

ccf_data <- combined_data[
  ,
  needed_columns,
  drop = FALSE
]

ccf_data$Date <- as.Date(ccf_data$Date)

# Average duplicate dates, if there are any
ccf_data <- aggregate(
  ccf_data[, -1, drop = FALSE],
  by = list(Date = ccf_data$Date),
  FUN = function(x) {
    if (all(is.na(x))) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  }
)

# Create a complete daily date sequence
daily_dates <- data.frame(
  Date = seq(
    min(ccf_data$Date),
    max(ccf_data$Date),
    by = "day"
  )
)

ccf_data <- merge(
  daily_dates,
  ccf_data,
  by = "Date",
  all.x = TRUE
)

ccf_data <- ccf_data[
  order(ccf_data$Date),
]
```

# Job openings only

## ARIMA. model

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(forecast)

# Number of days to forecast
forecast_horizon <- 36

# Readable names
job_labels <- c(
  DA  = "Data Analysis Job Openings",
  SW  = "Software Development Job Openings",
  ALL = "All Job Openings"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Fit separate univariate auto.arima models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

arima_models <- lapply(
  names(job_columns),
  function(job_name) {

    column_name <- job_columns[[job_name]]

    # Daily time series with weekly seasonality
    y <- ts(
      na.interp(combined_data[[column_name]]),
      frequency = 7
    )

    auto.arima(
      y,
      seasonal = TRUE,
      stepwise = FALSE,
      approximation = FALSE
    )
  }
)

names(arima_models) <- names(job_columns)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Forecast each series
# ------------------------------------------------------------

arima_forecasts <- lapply(
  arima_models,
  forecast,
  h = forecast_horizon,
  level = c(80, 95)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Prepare historical data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

historical_data <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(job_columns), function(job_name) {

    tibble(
      Date = combined_data$Date,
      Value = combined_data[[job_columns[[job_name]]]],
      Job_Type = job_labels[[job_name]]
    )
  })
) %>%
  drop_na(Value)

# Future dates
future_dates <- seq(
  max(combined_data$Date) + 1,
  by = "day",
  length.out = forecast_horizon
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Prepare forecast results
# ------------------------------------------------------------

forecast_data <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(arima_forecasts), function(job_name) {

    fc <- arima_forecasts[[job_name]]

    tibble(
      Date = future_dates,
      Forecast = as.numeric(fc$mean),
      Lower_80 = as.numeric(fc$lower[, "80%"]),
      Upper_80 = as.numeric(fc$upper[, "80%"]),
      Lower_95 = as.numeric(fc$lower[, "95%"]),
      Upper_95 = as.numeric(fc$upper[, "95%"]),
      Job_Type = job_labels[[job_name]]
    )
  })
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Plot historical values and forecasts
# ------------------------------------------------------------

arima_forecast_plot <- ggplot() +

  geom_line(
    data = historical_data,
    aes(
      x = Date,
      y = Value
    ),
    linewidth = 0.7,
    color = "#1F5A94"
  ) +

  geom_ribbon(
    data = forecast_data,
    aes(
      x = Date,
      ymin = Lower_95,
      ymax = Upper_95
    ),
    fill = "#9ECAE1",
    alpha = 0.35
  ) +

  geom_ribbon(
    data = forecast_data,
    aes(
      x = Date,
      ymin = Lower_80,
      ymax = Upper_80
    ),
    fill = "#4292C6",
    alpha = 0.40
  ) +

  geom_line(
    data = forecast_data,
    aes(
      x = Date,
      y = Forecast
    ),
    linewidth = 0.9,
    color = "#B2182B"
  ) +

  geom_vline(
    xintercept = max(combined_data$Date),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.6,
    color = "gray35"
  ) +

  facet_grid(
    Job_Type ~ .,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Univariate ARIMA Forecasts for Job Openings",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Separate auto.arima models with ",
      forecast_horizon,
      "-day forecasts"
    ),
    x = "Date",
    y = "Job-posting index",
    caption = paste0(
      "Red lines show forecasts. Dark and light shaded regions ",
      "represent 80% and 95% prediction intervals."
    )
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 18
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11,
      color = "gray35"
    ),
    strip.text = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 11
    ),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(
      hjust = 0,
      face = "italic"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(forecast)

# Number of observations used for testing
test_horizon <- 36

# Readable category names
job_labels <- c(
  DA  = "Data Analysis Job Openings",
  SW  = "Software Development Job Openings",
  ALL = "All Job Openings"
)

prediction_results <- list()
arima_test_models <- list()

for (job_name in names(job_columns)) {

  job_column <- job_columns[[job_name]]

  # Prepare the series
  series_data <- combined_data %>%
    select(
      Date,
      Value = all_of(job_column)
    ) %>%
    arrange(Date)

  # Interpolate missing observations
  full_series <- ts(
    forecast::na.interp(series_data$Value),
    frequency = 7
  )

  # Training and testing data
  train_series <- head(
    full_series,
    -test_horizon
  )

  test_series <- tail(
    full_series,
    test_horizon
  )

  test_dates <- tail(
    series_data$Date,
    test_horizon
  )

  # Fit auto.arima using only the training data
  model <- auto.arima(
    train_series,
    seasonal = TRUE,
    stepwise = FALSE,
    approximation = FALSE
  )

  # Predict the test period
  prediction <- forecast(
    model,
    h = test_horizon,
    level = c(80, 95)
  )

  # Save the model
  arima_test_models[[job_name]] <- model

  # Save actual and predicted values
  prediction_results[[job_name]] <- tibble(
    Date = test_dates,
    Actual = as.numeric(test_series),
    Predicted = as.numeric(prediction$mean),
    Lower_95 = as.numeric(prediction$lower[, "95%"]),
    Upper_95 = as.numeric(prediction$upper[, "95%"]),
    Job_Type = job_labels[[job_name]]
  )
}

# Combine the three results
actual_prediction_data <- bind_rows(
  prediction_results
)

# Plot actual versus predicted values
actual_vs_prediction_plot <- ggplot(
  actual_prediction_data,
  aes(x = Date)
) +

  # 95% prediction interval
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = Lower_95,
      ymax = Upper_95
    ),
    fill = "gray70",
    alpha = 0.35
  ) +

  # Actual values
  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = Actual,
      color = "Actual"
    ),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +

  geom_point(
    aes(
      y = Actual,
      color = "Actual"
    ),
    size = 1.5
  ) +

  # Predicted values
  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = Predicted,
      color = "Predicted"
    ),
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +

  geom_point(
    aes(
      y = Predicted,
      color = "Predicted"
    ),
    size = 1.5
  ) +

  facet_grid(
    Job_Type ~ .,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Actual" = "#1F5A94",
      "Predicted" = "#B2182B"
    )
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Actual Versus Predicted Job Openings",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Univariate auto.arima predictions for the final ",
      test_horizon,
      " days"
    ),
    x = "Date",
    y = "Job-posting index",
    color = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "Dashed red lines show predictions. ",
      "Shaded areas represent 95% prediction intervals."
    )
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 18
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11,
      color = "gray35"
    ),
    strip.text = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 11
    ),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.caption = element_text(
      hjust = 0,
      face = "italic"
    )
  )
```

## Prophet model

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(prophet)

# install.packages("prophet")  # Run once if Prophet is not installed

# Number of final observations used as the test period
test_horizon <- 36

# Readable category names
job_labels <- c(
  DA  = "Data Analysis Job Openings",
  SW  = "Software Development Job Openings",
  ALL = "All Job Openings"
)

prophet_models <- list()
prophet_predictions <- list()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Fit one Prophet model for each job-opening series
# ------------------------------------------------------------

for (job_name in names(job_columns)) {

  job_column <- job_columns[[job_name]]

  # Prophet requires columns named ds and y
  series_data <- combined_data %>%
    transmute(
      ds = as.Date(Date),
      y = as.numeric(.data[[job_column]])
    ) %>%
    arrange(ds) %>%
    filter(!is.na(y))

  # Split into training and testing periods
  train_data <- head(
    series_data,
    -test_horizon
  )

  test_data <- tail(
    series_data,
    test_horizon
  )

  # Fit the Prophet model using training data only
  model <- prophet(
    train_data,
    daily.seasonality = FALSE,
    weekly.seasonality = TRUE,
    yearly.seasonality = TRUE,
    interval.width = 0.95
  )

  # Predict the dates in the test period
  test_forecast <- predict(
    model,
    test_data %>%
      select(ds)
  )

  # Save fitted model
  prophet_models[[job_name]] <- model

  # Save actual and predicted values
  prophet_predictions[[job_name]] <- tibble(
    Date = test_data$ds,
    Actual = test_data$y,
    Predicted = test_forecast$yhat,
    Lower_95 = test_forecast$yhat_lower,
    Upper_95 = test_forecast$yhat_upper,
    Job_Type = job_labels[[job_name]]
  )
}

# Combine results from the three models
prophet_actual_prediction_data <- bind_rows(
  prophet_predictions
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot actual versus predicted values
# ------------------------------------------------------------

prophet_actual_vs_predicted_plot <- ggplot(
  prophet_actual_prediction_data,
  aes(x = Date)
) +

  # 95% prediction interval
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = Lower_95,
      ymax = Upper_95
    ),
    fill = "gray70",
    alpha = 0.35
  ) +

  # Actual values
  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = Actual,
      color = "Actual"
    ),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +

  geom_point(
    aes(
      y = Actual,
      color = "Actual"
    ),
    size = 1.5
  ) +

  # Prophet predictions
  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = Predicted,
      color = "Prophet Prediction"
    ),
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +

  geom_point(
    aes(
      y = Predicted,
      color = "Prophet Prediction"
    ),
    size = 1.5
  ) +

  facet_grid(
    Job_Type ~ .,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Actual" = "#1F5A94",
      "Prophet Prediction" = "#B2182B"
    )
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Actual Versus Predicted Job Openings",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Prophet predictions for the final ",
      test_horizon,
      " observations"
    ),
    x = "Date",
    y = "Job-posting index",
    color = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "Dashed red lines show Prophet predictions. ",
      "Shaded regions show 95% prediction intervals."
    )
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 18
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11,
      color = "gray35"
    ),
    strip.text = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 11
    ),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.caption = element_text(
      hjust = 0,
      face = "italic"
    )
  )
```

# ARIMAX: Regression + ARIMA errors

## Job Openings Vs. Stock Market

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(forecast)

# Number of final days used for testing
test_horizon <- 36

# Readable job-opening labels
job_labels <- c(
  DA  = "DA Job Openings",
  SW  = "SW Job Openings",
  ALL = "All Job Openings"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Prepare job-opening and stock-price data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

reg_arima_data <- combined_data %>%
  select(
    Date,
    all_of(unname(job_columns)),
    all_of(unname(stock_columns))
  ) %>%
  arrange(Date)

# Rename columns using the short object names
names(reg_arima_data)[
  match(unname(job_columns), names(reg_arima_data))
] <- names(job_columns)

names(reg_arima_data)[
  match(unname(stock_columns), names(reg_arima_data))
] <- names(stock_columns)

# Convert variables to numeric and interpolate missing values
reg_arima_data <- reg_arima_data %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      -Date,
      ~ forecast::na.interp(as.numeric(.x))
    )
  )

# Stop if the test period is too large
if (nrow(reg_arima_data) <= test_horizon + 36) {
  stop("There are not enough observations for this test horizon.")
}

# Stock-price predictor names
stock_predictors <- names(stock_columns)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Fit regression plus ARIMA-error models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

reg_arima_models <- list()
reg_arima_predictions <- list()

for (job_name in names(job_columns)) {

  number_observations <- nrow(reg_arima_data)
  training_end <- number_observations - test_horizon

  # Outcome series
  y <- reg_arima_data[[job_name]]

  # Stock-price regressors
  xreg <- as.matrix(
    reg_arima_data[
      ,
      stock_predictors,
      drop = FALSE
    ]
  )

  # Training and testing sets
  y_train <- ts(
    y[1:training_end],
    frequency = 7
  )

  y_test <- y[
    (training_end + 1):number_observations
  ]

  xreg_train <- xreg[
    1:training_end,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  xreg_test <- xreg[
    (training_end + 1):number_observations,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  test_dates <- reg_arima_data$Date[
    (training_end + 1):number_observations
  ]

  # Regression with auto-selected ARIMA errors
  model <- auto.arima(
    y_train,
    xreg = xreg_train,
    seasonal = TRUE,
    stepwise = FALSE,
    approximation = FALSE
  )

  # Predict the held-out period using its stock prices
  prediction <- forecast(
    model,
    xreg = xreg_test,
    h = test_horizon,
    level = 95
  )

  # Save the model
  reg_arima_models[[job_name]] <- model

  # Save actual and predicted values
  reg_arima_predictions[[job_name]] <- tibble(
    Date = test_dates,
    Actual = as.numeric(y_test),
    Predicted = as.numeric(prediction$mean),
    Lower_95 = as.numeric(prediction$lower[, "95%"]),
    Upper_95 = as.numeric(prediction$upper[, "95%"]),
    Job_Type = job_labels[[job_name]]
  )
}

# Combine results
reg_arima_prediction_data <- bind_rows(
  reg_arima_predictions
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Calculate test-set accuracy
# ------------------------------------------------------------

reg_arima_accuracy <- reg_arima_prediction_data %>%
  group_by(Job_Type) %>%
  summarise(
    RMSE = sqrt(
      mean((Actual - Predicted)^2)
    ),
    MAE = mean(
      abs(Actual - Predicted)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"

reg_arima_accuracy
```

## Job Openings Vs. Google Trends


```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(forecast)

# Number of final observations used for testing
test_horizon <- 36

# Short job-opening labels used in the plot
job_labels <- c(
  DA  = "DA Job Openings",
  SW  = "SW Job Openings",
  ALL = "All Job Openings"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Prepare job-opening and Google Trends data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

google_arima_data <- combined_data %>%
  select(
    Date,
    all_of(unname(job_columns)),
    all_of(unname(google_columns))
  ) %>%
  arrange(Date)

# Rename job-opening columns as DA, SW, and ALL
names(google_arima_data)[
  match(
    unname(job_columns),
    names(google_arima_data)
  )
] <- names(job_columns)

# Create safe names for Google Trends predictors
google_predictor_names <- make.names(
  names(google_columns),
  unique = TRUE
)

# Rename Google Trends columns
names(google_arima_data)[
  match(
    unname(google_columns),
    names(google_arima_data)
  )
] <- google_predictor_names

# Convert variables to numeric and interpolate missing values
google_arima_data <- google_arima_data %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      -Date,
      ~ forecast::na.interp(as.numeric(.x))
    )
  )

# Check that enough observations are available
if (nrow(google_arima_data) <= test_horizon + 36) {
  stop("There are not enough observations for the selected test period.")
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Define training and testing periods
# ------------------------------------------------------------

n_observations <- nrow(google_arima_data)

training_end <- n_observations - test_horizon

# Create lists for models and predictions
google_arima_models <- list()
google_arima_predictions <- list()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Fit regression models with ARIMA errors
# ------------------------------------------------------------

for (job_name in names(job_columns)) {

  # Job-opening outcome variable
  y <- google_arima_data[[job_name]]

  # Google Trends external regressors
  xreg <- as.matrix(
    google_arima_data[
      ,
      google_predictor_names,
      drop = FALSE
    ]
  )

  storage.mode(xreg) <- "double"

  # Training outcome
  y_train <- ts(
    y[1:training_end],
    frequency = 7
  )

  # Test outcome
  y_test <- y[
    (training_end + 1):n_observations
  ]

  # Training regressors
  xreg_train <- xreg[
    1:training_end,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  # Test regressors
  xreg_test <- xreg[
    (training_end + 1):n_observations,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  # Test-period dates
  test_dates <- google_arima_data$Date[
    (training_end + 1):n_observations
  ]

  # Fit regression with auto-selected ARIMA errors
  model <- auto.arima(
    y_train,
    xreg = xreg_train,
    seasonal = TRUE,
    stepwise = FALSE,
    approximation = FALSE
  )

  # Predict the held-out test period
  prediction <- forecast(
    model,
    xreg = xreg_test,
    h = test_horizon,
    level = 95
  )

  # Save model
  google_arima_models[[job_name]] <- model

  # Save actual and predicted values
  google_arima_predictions[[job_name]] <- tibble(
    Date = test_dates,
    Actual = as.numeric(y_test),
    Predicted = as.numeric(prediction$mean),
    Lower_95 = as.numeric(prediction$lower[, "95%"]),
    Upper_95 = as.numeric(prediction$upper[, "95%"]),
    Job_Type = job_labels[[job_name]]
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Combine prediction results
# ------------------------------------------------------------

google_arima_prediction_data <- bind_rows(
  google_arima_predictions
) %>%
  mutate(
    Job_Type = factor(
      Job_Type,
      levels = c(
        "All Job Openings",
        "DA Job Openings",
        "SW Job Openings"
      )
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Calculate test-period accuracy
# ------------------------------------------------------------

google_arima_accuracy <- google_arima_prediction_data %>%
  group_by(Job_Type) %>%
  summarise(
    RMSE = sqrt(
      mean(
        (Actual - Predicted)^2,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    ),

    MAE = mean(
      abs(Actual - Predicted),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    MAPE = mean(
      if_else(
        Actual != 0,
        abs((Actual - Predicted) / Actual),
        NA_real_
      ),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) * 100,

    .groups = "drop"
  )

google_arima_accuracy

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Plot actual versus predicted values
# ------------------------------------------------------------

google_arima_actual_vs_predicted_plot <- ggplot(
  google_arima_prediction_data,
  aes(x = Date)
) +

  # 95% prediction interval
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = Lower_95,
      ymax = Upper_95
    ),
    fill = "gray70",
    alpha = 0.30
  ) +

  # Actual values: solid blue line
  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = Actual,
      color = "Actual",
      linetype = "Actual"
    ),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +

  # Predicted values: dashed red line
  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = Predicted,
      color = "Predicted",
      linetype = "Predicted"
    ),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +

  facet_grid(
    Job_Type ~ .,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Actual" = "#1F5A94",
      "Predicted" = "#B2182B"
    )
  ) +

  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(
      "Actual" = "solid",
      "Predicted" = "dashed"
    )
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Actual Versus Predicted Job Openings",

    subtitle = paste0(
      "Regression with auto-selected ARIMA errors using ",
      "Google Trends search-interest variables"
    ),

    x = "Date",
    y = "Job-posting index",
    color = NULL,
    linetype = NULL,

    caption = paste0(
      "The final ",
      test_horizon,
      " observations were used as the test period. ",
      "Solid blue lines show actual values; dashed red lines show predictions. ",
      "Shaded regions represent 95% prediction intervals."
    )
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 18
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11,

    ),

    ),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
```

## Job Openings Vs. Google Trends

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(forecast)

# Number of final observations used for testing
test_horizon <- 36

# Labels for the three job-opening series
job_labels <- c(
  DA  = "DA Job Openings",
  SW  = "SW Job Openings",
  ALL = "All Job Openings"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Prepare job-opening and Google Trends data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

google_arima_data <- combined_data %>%
  select(
    Date,
    all_of(unname(job_columns)),
    all_of(unname(google_columns))
  ) %>%
  arrange(Date)

# Rename job-opening columns as DA, SW, ALL
names(google_arima_data)[
  match(unname(job_columns), names(google_arima_data))
] <- names(job_columns)

# Safe names for Google Trends predictors
google_predictor_names <- make.names(
  names(google_columns),
  unique = TRUE
)

# Rename Google Trends columns
names(google_arima_data)[
  match(unname(google_columns), names(google_arima_data))
] <- google_predictor_names

# Convert to numeric and interpolate missing values
google_arima_data <- google_arima_data %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      -Date,
      ~ forecast::na.interp(as.numeric(.x))
    )
  )

if (nrow(google_arima_data) <= test_horizon + 30) {
  stop("There are not enough observations for the selected test period.")
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Fit Regression + ARIMA errors and keep fitted + forecasted
# ------------------------------------------------------------

n_observations <- nrow(google_arima_data)
training_end <- n_observations - test_horizon

google_arima_models <- list()
google_arima_plot_data_list <- list()
google_arima_accuracy_list <- list()

for (job_name in names(job_columns)) {

  # Outcome variable
  y <- google_arima_data[[job_name]]

  # External regressors
  xreg <- as.matrix(
    google_arima_data[
      ,
      google_predictor_names,
      drop = FALSE
    ]
  )
  storage.mode(xreg) <- "double"

  # Train / test split
  y_train <- ts(
    y[1:training_end],
    frequency = 7
  )

  y_test <- y[
    (training_end + 1):n_observations
  ]

  xreg_train <- xreg[
    1:training_end,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  xreg_test <- xreg[
    (training_end + 1):n_observations,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  train_dates <- google_arima_data$Date[1:training_end]
  test_dates  <- google_arima_data$Date[(training_end + 1):n_observations]

  # Fit model
  model <- auto.arima(
    y_train,
    xreg = xreg_train,
    seasonal = TRUE,
    stepwise = FALSE,
    approximation = FALSE
  )

  # Training fitted values
  fitted_values <- as.numeric(fitted(model))

  # Test forecasts
  prediction <- forecast(
    model,
    xreg = xreg_test,
    h = test_horizon,
    level = 95
  )

  forecast_values <- as.numeric(prediction$mean)

  # Save model
  google_arima_models[[job_name]] <- model

  # Whole-period plotting data:
  # training = fitted values
  # testing  = forecasted values
  google_arima_plot_data_list[[job_name]] <- bind_rows(
    tibble(
      Date = train_dates,
      Actual = as.numeric(y[1:training_end]),
      Predicted = fitted_values,
      Period = "Training",
      Job_Type = job_labels[[job_name]]
    ),
    tibble(
      Date = test_dates,
      Actual = as.numeric(y_test),
      Predicted = forecast_values,
      Period = "Test",
      Job_Type = job_labels[[job_name]]
    )
  )

  # Accuracy only on test period
  google_arima_accuracy_list[[job_name]] <- tibble(
    Job_Type = job_labels[[job_name]],
    RMSE = sqrt(mean((y_test - forecast_values)^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
    MAE  = mean(abs(y_test - forecast_values), na.rm = TRUE),
    MAPE = mean(ifelse(y_test != 0,
                       abs((y_test - forecast_values) / y_test),
                       NA_real_), na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  )
}

# Combine all data
google_arima_plot_data <- bind_rows(google_arima_plot_data_list) %>%
  mutate(
    Job_Type = factor(
      Job_Type,
      levels = c(
        "All Job Openings",
        "DA Job Openings",
        "SW Job Openings"
      )
    )
  )

google_arima_accuracy <- bind_rows(google_arima_accuracy_list)
google_arima_accuracy

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Plot whole-series Actual vs Fitted/Predicted
# ------------------------------------------------------------
```

## JO VS. Stocks

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(forecast)

# Number of final observations used for testing
test_horizon <- 36

# Short job-opening labels
job_labels <- c(
  DA  = "DA Job Openings",
  SW  = "SW Job Openings",
  ALL = "All Job Openings"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Prepare job-opening and stock-price data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

stock_arima_data <- combined_data %>%
  select(
    Date,
    all_of(unname(job_columns)),
    all_of(unname(stock_columns))
  ) %>%
  arrange(Date)

# Rename job-opening columns as DA, SW, and ALL
names(stock_arima_data)[
  match(
    unname(job_columns),
    names(stock_arima_data)
  )
] <- names(job_columns)

# Create safe names for stock-price predictors
stock_predictor_names <- make.names(
  names(stock_columns),
  unique = TRUE
)

# Rename stock-price columns
names(stock_arima_data)[
  match(
    unname(stock_columns),
    names(stock_arima_data)
  )
] <- stock_predictor_names

# Convert variables to numeric and interpolate missing values
stock_arima_data <- stock_arima_data %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      -Date,
      ~ forecast::na.interp(as.numeric(.x))
    )
  )

# Check that enough observations are available
if (nrow(stock_arima_data) <= test_horizon + 30) {
  stop("There are not enough observations for the selected test period.")
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Define training and testing periods
# ------------------------------------------------------------

n_observations <- nrow(stock_arima_data)

training_end <- n_observations - test_horizon

stock_arima_models <- list()
stock_arima_plot_data_list <- list()
stock_arima_accuracy_list <- list()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Fit Regression + ARIMA-error models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

for (job_name in names(job_columns)) {

  # Job-opening outcome
  y <- stock_arima_data[[job_name]]

  # Stock-price regressors
  xreg <- as.matrix(
    stock_arima_data[
      ,
      stock_predictor_names,
      drop = FALSE
    ]
  )

  storage.mode(xreg) <- "double"

  # Training outcome
  y_train <- ts(
    y[1:training_end],
    frequency = 7
  )

  # Testing outcome
  y_test <- y[
    (training_end + 1):n_observations
  ]

  # Training regressors
  xreg_train <- xreg[
    1:training_end,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  # Testing regressors
  xreg_test <- xreg[
    (training_end + 1):n_observations,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  # Training and testing dates
  train_dates <- stock_arima_data$Date[
    1:training_end
  ]

  test_dates <- stock_arima_data$Date[
    (training_end + 1):n_observations
  ]

  # Fit regression with auto-selected ARIMA errors
  model <- auto.arima(
    y_train,
    xreg = xreg_train,
    seasonal = TRUE,
    stepwise = FALSE,
    approximation = FALSE
  )

  # Fitted values for the training period
  fitted_values <- as.numeric(
    fitted(model)
  )

  # Predictions for the testing period
  prediction <- forecast(
    model,
    xreg = xreg_test,
    h = test_horizon,
    level = 95
  )

  predicted_values <- as.numeric(
    prediction$mean
  )

  # Save the fitted model
  stock_arima_models[[job_name]] <- model

  # Combine training fitted values and test predictions
  stock_arima_plot_data_list[[job_name]] <- bind_rows(

    # Training period
    tibble(
      Date = train_dates,
      Actual = as.numeric(
        y[1:training_end]
      ),
      Fitted_Predicted = fitted_values,
      Period = "Training",
      Job_Type = job_labels[[job_name]]
    ),

    # Testing period
    tibble(
      Date = test_dates,
      Actual = as.numeric(y_test),
      Fitted_Predicted = predicted_values,
      Period = "Test",
      Job_Type = job_labels[[job_name]]
    )
  )

  # Test-set accuracy
  stock_arima_accuracy_list[[job_name]] <- tibble(
    Job_Type = job_labels[[job_name]],

    RMSE = sqrt(
      mean(
        (y_test - predicted_values)^2,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    ),

    MAE = mean(
      abs(y_test - predicted_values),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    MAPE = mean(
      ifelse(
        y_test != 0,
        abs(
          (y_test - predicted_values) / y_test
        ),
        NA_real_
      ),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) * 100
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Combine results
# ------------------------------------------------------------

stock_arima_plot_data <- bind_rows(
  stock_arima_plot_data_list
) %>%
  mutate(
    Job_Type = factor(
      Job_Type,
      levels = c(
        "All Job Openings",
        "DA Job Openings",
        "SW Job Openings"
      )
    )
  )

stock_arima_accuracy <- bind_rows(

stock_arima_accuracy
```

# 3 models

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(forecast)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Function to extract the ARIMA/SARIMA order
# ------------------------------------------------------------

extract_arima_model <- function(model, predictor_group, job_name) {

  model_order <- forecast::arimaorder(model)

  p <- unname(model_order[1])
  d <- unname(model_order[2])
  q <- unname(model_order[3])

  # Seasonal orders are zero when auto.arima selects
  # a nonseasonal error structure
  P <- if (length(model_order) >= 6) unname(model_order[4]) else 0
  D <- if (length(model_order) >= 6) unname(model_order[5]) else 0
  Q <- if (length(model_order) >= 6) unname(model_order[6]) else 0

  seasonal_period <- 7

  model_label <- if (P == 0 && D == 0 && Q == 0) {

    paste0(
      "Regression + ARIMA(",
      p, ",", d, ",", q,
      ") errors"
    )

  } else {

    paste0(
      "Regression + SARIMA(",
      p, ",", d, ",", q,
      ")(",
      P, ",", D, ",", Q,
      ")[", seasonal_period, "] errors"
    )
  }

  tibble(
    Predictor_Group = predictor_group,

    Job_Openings = recode(
      job_name,
      "DA"  = "DA Job Openings",
      "SW"  = "SW Job Openings",
      "ALL" = "All Job Openings",
      .default = job_name
    ),

    p = p,
    d = d,
    q = q,
    P = P,
    D = D,
    Q = Q,
    Seasonal_Period = seasonal_period,
    Selected_Model = model_label,

    AICc = if (
      is.null(model$aicc)
    ) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      model$aicc
    }
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Combine the three sets of models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

model_sets <- list(
  "Stock Prices" = stock_arima_models,
  "Google Trends" = google_arima_models,
  "CAPEX + PPI" = economic_arima_models
)

sarima_model_summary <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  model_sets,
  function(models, predictor_group) {

    purrr::imap_dfr(
      models,
      function(model, job_name) {

        extract_arima_model(
          model = model,
          predictor_group = predictor_group,
          job_name = job_name
        )
      }
    )
  }
)

# Order the table
sarima_model_summary <- sarima_model_summary %>%
  mutate(
    Predictor_Group = factor(
      Predictor_Group,
      levels = c(
        "Stock Prices",
        "Google Trends",
        "CAPEX + PPI"
      )
    ),

    Job_Openings = factor(
      Job_Openings,
      levels = c(
        "All Job Openings",
        "DA Job Openings",
        "SW Job Openings"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    Predictor_Group,
    Job_Openings
  )

# Display selected models
sarima_model_summary %>%
  select(
    Predictor_Group,
    Job_Openings,
    Selected_Model,
    AICc
  )
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Function to extract the exact model description
# ------------------------------------------------------------

extract_model_description <- function(model) {

  model_output <- capture.output(
    print(model)
  )

  model_line <- model_output[
    grepl(
      "Regression with ARIMA|ARIMA\\(",
      model_output
    )
  ][1]

  trimws(model_line)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Create table for all nine models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

selected_arima_models <- bind_rows(

  # Stock-price models
  purrr::imap_dfr(
    stock_arima_models,
    function(model, job_name) {

      tibble(
        Predictor_Group = "Stock Prices",
        Job_Openings = job_name,
        Selected_Model = extract_model_description(model)
      )
    }
  ),

  # Google Trends models
  purrr::imap_dfr(
    google_arima_models,
    function(model, job_name) {

      tibble(
        Predictor_Group = "Google Trends",
        Job_Openings = job_name,
        Selected_Model = extract_model_description(model)
      )
    }
  ),

  # CAPEX and PPI models
  purrr::imap_dfr(
    economic_arima_models,
    function(model, job_name) {

      tibble(
        Predictor_Group = "CAPEX + PPI",
        Job_Openings = job_name,
        Selected_Model = extract_model_description(model)
      )
    }
  )
) %>%

  # Add readable job-opening labels
  mutate(
    Job_Openings = recode(
      Job_Openings,
      "ALL" = "All Job Openings",
      "DA"  = "DA Job Openings",
      "SW"  = "SW Job Openings"
    ),

    Predictor_Group = factor(
      Predictor_Group,
      levels = c(
        "Stock Prices",
        "Google Trends",
        "CAPEX + PPI"
      )
    ),

    Job_Openings = factor(
      Job_Openings,
      levels = c(
        "All Job Openings",
        "DA Job Openings",
        "SW Job Openings"
      )
    )
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    Predictor_Group,
    Job_Openings
  )
```

# Traditional Vs. DL

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(forecast)

compare_dm <- function(
  arima_data,
  dl_data,
  dl_model_name,
  forecast_horizon = 1
) {

  comparison_data <- arima_data %>%
    select(
      Date,
      Job_Type,
      Actual,
      ARIMA_Predicted = Predicted
    ) %>%
    inner_join(
      dl_data %>%
        select(
          Date,
          Job_Type,
          DL_Predicted = Predicted
        ),
      by = c(
        "Date",
        "Job_Type"
      )
    ) %>%
    drop_na(
      Actual,
      ARIMA_Predicted,
      DL_Predicted
    )

  comparison_results <- comparison_data %>%
    group_by(Job_Type) %>%
    group_modify(
      ~ {

        arima_errors <- .x$Actual - .x$ARIMA_Predicted
        dl_errors <- .x$Actual - .x$DL_Predicted

        dm_result <- forecast::dm.test(
          e1 = arima_errors,
          e2 = dl_errors,
          alternative = "two.sided",
          h = forecast_horizon,
          power = 2
        )

        arima_rmse <- sqrt(
          mean(arima_errors^2)
        )

        dl_rmse <- sqrt(
          mean(dl_errors^2)
        )

        mean_loss_difference <- mean(
          arima_errors^2 - dl_errors^2
        )

        tibble(
          DL_Model = dl_model_name,
          N = length(arima_errors),
          ARIMA_RMSE = arima_rmse,
          DL_RMSE = dl_rmse,
          Mean_Loss_Difference = mean_loss_difference,
          DM_Statistic = unname(dm_result$statistic),
          P_Value = dm_result$p.value,
          Better_Model = case_when(
            mean_loss_difference < 0 ~
              "Regression + ARIMA errors",
            mean_loss_difference > 0 ~
              dl_model_name,
            TRUE ~ "Equal"
          ),
          Significant = if_else(
            dm_result$p.value < 0.05,
            "Yes",
            "No"
          )
        )
      }
    ) %>%
    ungroup()

  comparison_results
}
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
stock_dm_results <- stock_dm_data %>%
  group_by(Model) %>%
  group_modify(
    ~ {

      # Paired forecast errors
      sarimax_errors <-
        .x$SARIMAX_Actual -
        .x$SARIMAX_Predicted

      dl_errors <-
        .x$DL_Actual -
        .x$DL_Predicted

      # Diebold-Mariano test
      dm_result <- forecast::dm.test(
        e1 = sarimax_errors,
        e2 = dl_errors,
        alternative = "two.sided",
        h = 1,
        power = 2
      )

      # Accuracy measures
      sarimax_rmse <- sqrt(
        mean(
          sarimax_errors^2,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
      )

      dl_rmse <- sqrt(
        mean(
          dl_errors^2,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
      )

      sarimax_mae <- mean(
        abs(sarimax_errors),
        na.rm = TRUE
      )

      dl_mae <- mean(
        abs(dl_errors),
        na.rm = TRUE
      )

      # SARIMAX squared loss minus DL squared loss
      mean_loss_difference <- mean(
        sarimax_errors^2 -
          dl_errors^2,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )

      tibble(
        N = length(sarimax_errors),

        SARIMAX_RMSE = sarimax_rmse,
        DL_RMSE = dl_rmse,

        SARIMAX_MAE = sarimax_mae,
        DL_MAE = dl_mae,

        Mean_Loss_Difference =
          mean_loss_difference,

        DM_Statistic = unname(
          dm_result$statistic
        ),

        P_Value = dm_result$p.value,

        Lower_Loss_Model = case_when(
          mean_loss_difference < 0 ~
            "SARIMAX",

          mean_loss_difference > 0 ~
            .y$Model[[1]],

          TRUE ~ "Equal"
        ),

        Significant = if_else(
          dm_result$p.value < 0.05,
          "Yes",
          "No"
        )
      )
    }
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

stock_dm_results
```

```{r}
stock_dm_table <- stock_dm_results %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        SARIMAX_RMSE,
        DL_RMSE,
        SARIMAX_MAE,
        DL_MAE,
        Mean_Loss_Difference
      ),
      ~ round(.x, 4)
    ),

    DM_Statistic = round(
      DM_Statistic,
      3
    ),

    `p-value` = format.pval(
      P_Value,
      digits = 3,
      eps = 0.001
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    Job_Openings = Model,
    N,
    SARIMAX_RMSE,
    DL_RMSE,
    SARIMAX_MAE,
    DL_MAE,
    DM_Statistic,
    `p-value`,
    Lower_Loss_Model,
    Significant
  ) %>%
  rename(
    `DL Model` = Job_Openings
  )
```
